sourceObservations: The original shows a bright golden, polygonal ribbed lantern cage against a compact brown support and base. Five gold ribs and the dark end-cap structure are identity features, not decoration to remove.

The native builder describes a square plinth, upright post, forward overhang, hanging hook, octagonal paper body, five ribs and two dark wood caps. The prominent upright shape in this projection must not be redesigned into an unrelated handle or freestanding lamp.
The original uses very sharp yellow/orange edge bands and abrupt face-to-face shading. The wooden base reads as a largely dark block, with limited warm surface volume.

The golden body is legible, but the hard faceted surface and narrow bright edges feel less soft and rounded than the selected target. Softness should come from controlled broad transitions while retaining the original silhouette and construction.
targetObservations: The target provides broad honey-yellow light transitions across the ribs and paper body, softened bevels at corners, and a warmer brown base with more visible face and edge volume.
Its warm highlights stay compatible with golden yellow and amber wood. The desirable result is a bright lantern with gentle internal illumination and distinguishable structural layers.

The target changes canvas occupancy and apparent proportions relative to the original and includes bright edge/fringe pixels. Its padding, silhouette inflation, local shape drift and any halo are not registration or geometry authority.
A single target facing cannot establish hidden construction. The other native facings must remain coherent manifestations of the actual model.
